title: Water from the Well of Bethlehem
reflectionText: David said longingly, “Oh that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem!” The three broke through the army of the Philistines and brought it to him. He would not drink it, but poured it out to Yahweh, saying it was the blood of the men who risked their lives. Whose costly gift could you honor?
editorialNotes: Packet 036 initial writer output. Short-only owner plan. The retelling remains within 2 Samuel 23:13-23 and follows 1438 (2 Samuel 23:8-12). Verse 17’s “He said”/“And he said” names David. It keeps WEB stronghold/“said longingly”/army/“risked their lives”/“the two sons of Ariel of Moab”/“a huge Egyptian” and KJV hold/longed/host/“went in jeopardy of their lives”/“two lionlike men of Moab”/“an Egyptian, a goodly man” in their own lanes. Verse 19 keeps WEB “he wasn’t included as one of the three” and KJV “he attained not unto the first three”. It ends with David setting Benaiah over his guard in verse 23.
